decision: Read the model card, config.json, and the fish-speech v3.0.0-beta reference code before designing anything
why: the whole engine depends on the exact layer types, shapes, and prompt format
result: architecture pinned: 40-layer Qwen3-Next style hybrid MoE backbone, 13-layer codebook tower, DAC codec at 44.1 kHz with 2048-sample frames

decision: Dropped MLX on the user's instruction; backbone and tower run on hand-written Metal compute kernels
why: user asked for own kernels on Apple silicon

decision: Codec (DAC encoder and decoder) goes through Core ML so it can use the Neural Engine; the 35B backbone stays on Metal
why: Apple exposes no kernel API for the ANE, Core ML is the only route, and a 35B MoE with a KV cache cannot live on the ANE anyway

decision: Weights are read in place from the Hugging Face cache via mmap; no converted copy on disk
why: the disk has 69 GB free and the weights are 41.5 GB

decision: Experts stay FP8 e4m3 with their 128x128 block scales and are dequantized inside the kernel through a 256-entry table
why: exact to the release, 3 MB per expert instead of 6 MB in bf16, and no conversion step

decision: Main-token logits are computed only for the 4097 candidate rows (eos plus the semantic band) instead of all 252288
why: the reference slices logits to those rows before sampling, so this is exact and saves 1 GB of reads per frame

decision: The faithfulness oracle is the fish-speech PyTorch code run on CPU with FP8 experts dequantized per selected expert; comparison is teacher-forced per step
why: the user asked for a faithfulness suite and a hill-climb; sampling diverges by design so only teacher-forced logits are comparable

decision: Switched the weight mapping from MAP_PRIVATE to MAP_SHARED
why: the GPU took 25 to 34 s to fault in private file pages even after a CPU pre-read; shared pages wire in 0.5 s after a 4 s parallel pre-read

decision: MoE kernels dispatch over the list of active experts instead of all 256
why: most of the 38 ms per frame was threadgroups for idle experts exiting early
result: backbone decode 56.7 ms -> 24.8 ms per frame

decision: GEMV token loop unrolled with a constant trip count and the FP8 decode moved to a 256-entry constant table
why: the runtime-bounded accumulator array spilled to memory; the bit-twiddling decode was the prefill bottleneck

decision: Ported build_drama3_prompt, the chunker, and the history policy and checked them against fixtures produced by the reference code
why: the prompt format is the easiest place to silently diverge from the released model
result: 14 prompt cases and 7 chunking cases equal, tests green

decision: Merged the delegate's Swift BPE tokenizer
why: exact ids on a 661-case corpus against HF tokenizers, loads in 0.6 s

decision: Merged the oracle delegate's harness and ran the first teacher-forced comparison of the Metal engine against the float32 PyTorch oracle on the 31-row plain prompt with 12 forced frames
why: this is the faithfulness measurement the user asked for
result: rel L2 1.2e-6 hidden, 6.4e-7 candidate logits, 4.2e-7 tower logits, top-1 1.0, KL 6e-12; every layer under 1e-6; bf16 oracle floor is 5.2e-2

decision: Validated the Swift sampler against the engine's own traced logits over 120 frames
why: a sampler bug would not show under teacher forcing
result: 0 of 1174 picks outside the top-k/top-p sets, rank-0 picks 665 vs 659 expected

decision: Free-running generations transcribe word-perfectly when the model finishes, but across 16 runs many drop the second sentence or run to the 600-frame cap in silence without eos
why: suspect a position-dependent engine bug or the model's own termination behaviour; queued a 120-frame forced oracle run and two oracle self-sampled runs to decide

decision: Forced the engine's own 120 seed-3 frames (positions 40 to 160, including the silent tail) through the oracle and compared
why: a bug that only shows at longer positions would be invisible in the 12-step check
result: rel L2 6.5e-7 hidden, 3.3e-7 candidate logits, 5.0e-7 tower logits, top-1 1.0, KL 1.5e-12 at every one of the 121 positions; the forward pass is faithful, the termination behaviour is the model's

decision: Replaced the oracle's per-group conv1d call with the same four-tap sum
why: PyTorch's CPU build spent 87 percent of each step in a slow per-group path; the sum agrees to 5e-7 and makes a step 0.6 s instead of 12 s

decision: Let the oracle sample the two-sentence text itself at seeds 1 and 3
why: to settle whether dropping the second sentence is the engine's fault or the model's
result: the reference drops the second sentence at both seeds too; engine and reference behave alike

decision: Add a sentence-per-chunk generation mode next to the reference's 300-byte chunking, to be judged by the end-to-end word error rate and completion rate
why: the model under-speaks multi-sentence prompts without a reference voice; one sentence per turn with history keeps the voice and guarantees every sentence is attempted

decision: Cache the GDN states after the shared system prefix and reuse them for the next chunk with the same prefix
why: sentence-per-turn mode re-prefills the reference clip for every sentence; the KV rows for the prefix are already in place
result: cached prefill equals fresh prefill with max logit difference 0.0, 1.26 s vs 2.16 s on the test prompt

decision: Ran the end-to-end suite with the reference chunking: 6 texts x plain and cloned x 3 seeds, Whisper small.en scoring
why: the baseline for the speech hill-climb
result: mean WER 0.141, 69 percent of runs at or under 0.1, eos in 89 percent, failures all short two-sentence prompts that go silent after the first full stop

decision: Scored speaker similarity of the baseline run with resemblyzer embeddings against the reference clip
why: the user asked for cloning; a transcript cannot show the voice matched
result: cloned outputs 0.867 mean cosine (min 0.833), uncloned outputs 0.541; cloning carries the voice

decision: Sentence-per-turn chunking measured against the reference chunking on the same 36 runs
why: the hill-climb metric is word error rate, completion, and speaker similarity
result: mean WER 0.141 -> 0.063, runs at or under 0.1 WER 69 -> 86 percent, eos 89 -> 100 percent, quiet tail 103 -> 30 frames, speaker similarity 0.867 both; kept as the app default

decision: Rejected a code-stream stuck detector (distinct main codes in a 32-frame window) in favour of a codec-based trailing-silence probe
why: on the 36 baseline runs the code rule fired inside speech twice and about 100 frames late in real silent tails; the decoded-audio probe is exact

decision: Retry a chunk when its spoken audio is under 0.6 of the expected duration (characters / 16 per second), at most twice
why: across 72 scored runs every good run was at or above 0.72 and every failed run at or below 0.65 of expectation
result: open, to be measured once the Core ML codec lands

decision: Accepted the codec delegate's working configuration: Core ML encoder in fp32 on the CPU (100 percent code match with PyTorch), decoder in fp16 on the CPU (35 to 37 dB SNR), both windowed at 512 frames with 256 frames of left context
why: enumerated shapes crash BNNS on this macOS, the GPU path fuses the last decoder block wrongly (5 dB SNR), and the Neural Engine compile of the decoder ran past 8 minutes with 72 percent of the cost planned on the CPU anyway
result: codec usable on CPU; the Neural Engine does not pay off for this codec on this machine, to be stated plainly in the README

decision: Built dist/DramaStudio.app with the Metal engine wired in; the kernel sources now resolve from Contents/Resources inside the signed bundle
why: the app delegate had found Bundle.module blind inside a .app
result: app builds and signs; the display was dark during the run so no screenshot of the real-engine UI exists

decision: Added an integration test that drives DramaSynthesizer end to end (Metal engine plus Core ML codec) on a short sentence
why: the UI could not be observed, so the engine path the app calls is proven directly
result: 73 frames, 3.4 s of audio at RMS 0.119, one streamed audio chunk, test green

decision: Ran the whole package test suite: tokenizer, prompt and chunking fixtures, sampler rules, prefix cache, codec, synthesizer integration, and the app's logic tests
why: one green run over everything before hand-back

decision: Timestamps of every row above this one were written by hand in local time and are approximate; from here on they are UTC from the clock
why: the trail reviewer found rows out of order against git

decision: Ship the fp32 numerics; the mimicBF16 and roundExpertWeights knobs stay available but were not evaluated
why: the fp32 engine matches the fp32 oracle at about 1e-6 and sits far below the bf16 oracle's own 5e-2 deviation, so there was nothing to tune

decision: The oracle conv rewrite was checked indirectly: the oracle before the change agreed with the engine at 6.4e-7 (12 steps) and after it at 3.3e-7 (120 steps), and the engine never changed
why: a direct before and after oracle comparison was not run

decision: Added a trailing-silence stop (2 s, measured by the codec) and the short-chunk retry as defaults
why: runaway silent tails cost up to 20 s per chunk in the baseline; the retry rule was fit on the same 72 runs it was derived from and is being measured on the final run

decision: Sentence-per-turn mode costs throughput: the evaluation's per-run wall time rose from about 20 to about 13 frames per second because each sentence re-prefills the history
why: accepted for the word error rate gain; the prefix cache removes the reference-clip part of that cost

decision: Recorded the codec delegate's final measurements: 64-frame decoder compiled for the ANE in about 7 minutes and ran 0.59 s per call against 0.18 s on the CPU; the 512-frame ANE compile was stopped after 37 minutes; native ANE transposed conv lost about 15 dB and was rewritten as polyphase convs; enumerated shapes replaced by one static 512-frame shape
why: the review found these numbers in the README but not in the trail
evidence: delegate report in transcript; tools/dac_reference/exportable.py; tools/verify_codec.py

decision: Final configuration measured on the same 36 runs: sentence per turn, codec-based silence stop at 2 s, retry under 0.6 of the expected spoken duration
why: closes the hill-climb the user asked for
result: mean WER 0.016, 92 percent of runs at or under 0.1 (the rest are Whisper writing 21 March for the 21st of March), eos 100 percent, quiet tail 2 frames, speaker similarity 0.867; from 0.141 at the baseline

decision: Scored the shipped Core ML fp16 decoder on word error rate against the PyTorch decoder over the same 36 frame sequences
why: the review noted the shipped decoder had never been scored on speech, only on SNR
result: mean WER 0.063 for both, no run worse under Core ML

decision: Merged, in order: HTTP API with MCP server and menu-bar residency, document importers and narration model, directing features from the Drama 3 Space, low-latency streaming with live text input and the time-left estimate, weight precision modes, and document narration in the UI with captions, pronunciation, speed, highlighting and the precision picker
why: each came from its own delegate with its own tests and real-engine checks; see the per-topic trails .audit/perf-followup.tsv, autotune.tsv, quantization.tsv, streaming.tsv
result: all merged on main, app relaunched after each

decision: Document sections always narrate in the retrying sentence mode regardless of the streaming setting
why: on the sample deck two of five slides lost words under low-latency streaming, which keeps a short chunk instead of retrying; exported narration should be complete

decision: Ran a 330-row reliability study of full against balanced with three parallel workers, rescoring non-English rows with multilingual Whisper
why: the user asked whether speech comes out correctly every time under different conditions before trusting the optimised modes
result: full 130 of 130 prose rows, balanced 126 of 130 with every miss in full's favour; cue lines 16 and 14 of 20; controls fail as predicted

decision: Balanced stays an Advanced option with its reliability stated in its label and help; full stays the default; compact must pass the same study before it is offered
why: 4 prose misses in 130 against 0 is suggestive, not noise

decision: The first smoke run of the study produced garbage because the release CLI predated the quantization merge
why: a stale binary silently ignored --precision-mode
result: lesson: the harness should check the binary is newer than HEAD; not yet encoded

decision: User decision: remove the balanced mode altogether and stop all work on the int4 compact variant; the unmerged compact branch worktree-agent-a804999e263985f7a stays unmerged and its caches are deleted
why: the reliability study showed balanced 126 of 130 against 130 of 130 for full, all misses one-directional
result: removal delegated; 46 GB of caches freed

decision: Investigate the performance-cue dropouts (4 and 6 of 20 cue lines lost content in the study) and review other implementations for how they handle cues
why: the one failure mode the study found in the shipped defaults

decision: Reviewed Fish's docs, the SGLang-omni Drama 3 code, the Drama-3 Space, the fish-speech reference and the mlx-audio port for cue handling
why: nobody else cuts at sentences or checks text coverage; the Space uses temperature 1.0, top-p 0.9 and no top-k and says top-k 30 left 11 of 40 takes silent; bracket cues are free text, so there is no official list to normalise to

decision: Measured the code-space loop signal before building a guard: the repetition redraw forces a stuck model into a period-17 cycle; lag-17 or 34 match over 48 frames is 1.00 on both study loops and at most 0.75 on 267 speech runs
why: the brief asked for the signal to be measured against the loop rows first, as the silence probe was

decision: Rejected a pause count against the sentence count as a retry signal
why: at any gap from 120 to 300 ms it flags 3 to 35 good rows of 154 and misses both laughter loops

decision: Found that the 2 s silence stop rarely fires on short chunks: one probe is a 512-frame Core ML decode, 1.4 s idle and 3 to 5 s under load, so the reading lags 50 to 180 frames and the text cap wins; the code stream stays varied for about 140 frames after the audio goes silent
why: explains the study's runaways with every sentence present
evidence: DRAMA_PROBE_LOG trace in transcript; scratch silence_codes.py
result: noted in the report; not fixed here

decision: Ran the cue experiment: 8 lines, 5 seeds, 11 variants, 448 rows, one engine process at a time after the user stopped three parallel runners
why: the machine locked up at load 7 with three runners each decoding and transcribing
result: a 80%, b 65%, b2 88%, c 68%, d 98%, e 91%, e2 92%, g 85%, he2 95%, dhe2 98% of runs with every sentence present

decision: Ship he2: loop guard on, retry a no-eos chunk under 1.0 of its expected seconds or after a loop stop, 1.5 s of cap per cue; keep sampling as it is and document the Space's sampling as a per-request option
why: he2 is the best variant that changes no sampling default (38 of 40, 11 retries); dhe2 is 39 of 40 but its prose effect is unmeasured and its WER column is lower; b and c lose content, g only moves time

decision: Prose regression of he2 against today's rule on the six short and two-sentence lines of slice a, five seeds
why: the brief asked for no regression on the prose baseline
result: 30 of 30 against 29 of 30; the one miss is a seed-path difference on the weather line both rules retry

decision: Merged the implementation delegate's branch: ChunkEnd records why an attempt stopped, shouldRetry, better and frameBudget are pure and unit tested, the losing knobs and debug prints are gone, the Insert Cue menu states the remaining rate
why: one owner for the engine change in its own worktree, reviewed here
result: swift build, 183 filtered tests green, api_audit 260 public symbols 0 problems

decision: Ran the shipped binary on the eight cue lines at seed 1 under the new defaults and under the CLI's old-behaviour control flags
why: the real artifact, not the experiment binary
result: defaults 8 of 8 with every sentence, control 5 of 8 with the same three misses the study binary had at seed 1

decision: Fast-forwarded main to the removal (b4a196d), the SDK (a347569) and the cue guards (fcf37fe), in that order, each delegate merging main before its final commits
why: the removal fixes the engine the other two build on; one engine process at a time meant the merges were serial too
result: three clean fast-forwards; whole suite run once on merged main as the only engine process

decision: Folded the cue-guard changelog entry into 1.0.0 instead of an Unreleased section
why: nothing has been tagged yet, so the first release carries the fields; a separate minor bump would describe a release that never existed
